text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

JOHN CHURCHILL, the DUKE OF MARLBOROUGH was born in 1650. As a statesman he was highly regarded in England, but as a General he became a national hero. He's considered one of the ten best generals in all of history.

English blacksmith boxer ROBERT FITZSIMMONS was born in 1863. He was raised in New Zealand, and gained fame for knocking out World middleweight champion JACK DEMPSEY. He was known as the 'The Freckled Freak'.
Conductor EUGENE GOOSSENS was born in 1893. He became famous for his work with the Sydney Symphony orchestra.

American actor JOHN WAYNE was born in 1907. He first came to notice in the film 'Stagecoach', after which he became 'the' star of western films. His other movies included 'The Searchers', 'The Shootist', 'The Green Berets", and 'The Alamo'. He won an oscar for his role in 'True Grit'. He died of cancer in 1979.

US singer PEGGY LEE was born in 1920. Her real name was NORMA DELORES EGSTROM. In 1941 BENNY GOODMAN signed PEGGY up for his band. Hits included "Somebody Else Is Taking My Place" (1942) and "Why Don't You Do Right?" (1943). She had success as a solo artist from 1945 on with hits such as "Lover" (1952), "Mr Wonderful" (1956), "Fever" (1958) and "Is That All There Is?" (1969).

Political lobbyist and Labor party figure DAVID COMBE was born in 1943. He became famous first as National Labor Party Secretary, and then because he'd had dealings with a Russian diplomat, later accused of spying.

Fleetwood Mac singer STEVIE NICKS was born in 1948. She began her career as a member of the group 'Fritz' with LINDSEY BUCKINGHAM. They worked as a duo before joining 'Fleetwood Mac' in 1975. "Rumours" - the 1977 album was a giant hit selling more than 25 million copies. STEVIE launched a solo career with hits such as "Stop Draggin' My Heart Around" (1981), "Stand Back" (1983), "Talk To Me" (1985) and "Rooms On Fire" (1989).
Australian weightlifting champion DEAN LUKIN was born in 1960. The South Australian tuna fisherman won a gold medal at the Los Angeles Olympics. He now runs a designer fashion label.
** EVENTS **

1865 : Confederate General Kirby Smith surrendered his forces in Louisiana and ended the American Civil War. While the official surrender was signed weeks before, Smith's army was the last active Southern unit to stop fighting. The war killed over half a million Americans.
1880 : An amazing cricket match happened in Cambridge. In the one day the Cambridge 12 managed to score 593. In reply their opponents the Gentlemen of England scored 232.
1923 : A new era of motor racing was born at Le Mans in France. Local drivers Lagache and Leonard became the first to win the famous 24 hour race.
1933 : Following the exploration efforts of MAWSON, Australia claimed one third of Antarctica.
1940 : 700 boats set sail from Britain to evacuate Allied troops trapped by the Germans at Dunkirk in France.
1979 : Israel formally returned the Sinai to Egypt, as part of the peace deal worked out by ANWAR SADAT.
1988 : The White-dominated National Party celebrated 40 years in office in South Africa.

1991 : A Lauda-Air airliner crashed into the jungle in Thailand. 223 people were killed. The plane was bound for Austria, and was the first plane lost by the airline, which was owned by former racing car driver NICKI LAUDA.
1994 : BRONWYN BISHOP was named as Opposition Health spokesman in ALEXANDER DOWNER's shadow cabinet.
